## Setup

Hydrate isolated worktrees under .worktrees/ with `uv sync --frozen`; use
`work-link --ensure .venv` for the synced checkout. Never use live `setup.sh`
as development hydration. Follow [development](docs/development.md).

## Gates

Use `just test-one <runner> <args...>` for changed behavior: runners are pytest,
zsh and nvim, with literal argument forwarding. Run `just check-hygiene` for
mandatory ops-check, format, syntax, link/modeline, promoted-glass, guide and record checks.
Use `just docs` after changing identity; `python3 tools/ops-docs check` checks drift.

The validated `.tt.toml` disables automatic broad test, check-code and
portable-test requests. Skips start no child, record null outcomes and are never
passes. Missing policy enables broad work; invalid policy fails. Focused checks
and hygiene always run; prose-only changes need no new tests. Incomplete automatic
integration coverage and delayed discovery are accepted for this personal config.
Known failures still require a fix or explicit disposition.

Deliberate full verification uses `just test-full`, `TT_FORCE=1 just check`, or
`TT_FORCE=1 just test-portable`. No fast selector is claimed. For shell/editor
bootstrap, setup, hooks, Noctalia or host interaction changes, select an affected
explicit integration check before live use. A policy skip proves neither suite
correctness nor host health. `verify` includes actual host inspection.

Portable CI covers seven fake-host Python modules, not the full suite, desktop,
GPU, systemd or installed console behavior. `just ci-hygiene` omits private records
and live promoted state. `ci_suite_refs` remains empty. Local hook installation,
workflow publication and host activation require their own authority; merging
source installs no hooks. Hosted broad work must explicitly set TT_FORCE=1.
See development for the exact CI contract, excluded work and evidence limits.

## Layout

- `setup.sh`, `install.toml`, `install-linux.toml`, `install-graphical.toml`, `lib/` — host installer and link manifests.
- `bin/`, `shell/`, `nvim/`, `kitty/`, `niri/`, `noctalia/`, `systemd/` — commands and configuration.
- `docs/` — eight current subject references.
- `tests/` — focused and full test suites and their fixtures.
- `scripts/` — the repository's own gates and maintenance scripts (hygiene, code
  checks, test front doors, agent-session probes).
- `tools/` — copies vendored from ops (`tt`, `ops-check`, `ops-docs`, the code
  organization guide); never edited here.

Code-organization deviations (most of the tree is per-application configuration,
not a source tree):

- `setup.sh` stays at the root: it is the documented bootstrap entry
  (`.ops-check.toml` `root_sources_allowed`).
- No src/ package tree: `bin/` holds self-contained commands and `shell/` holds
  sourced shell configuration; neither is an importable package.
- `lib/` keeps its name: it holds the data files that setup, health and hygiene source
  and the Git packing policy they run, not a grab-bag module.
- `tools/` remains the home of vendored ops copies, where ops's tooling writes them.
- Machine layout is allowed in the configuration, installer, references and fixtures
  listed in `.ops-check.toml` `layout_allowed`: the dotfiles create that layout.

## Rules

- Update subject references when their source behavior changes. Keep public docs
  current, undated and free of task IDs or private evidence locators. Historical
  decisions and plans belong in records, not the public reference directory.
- Preserve functional cheatsheets, copied plugin provenance and vendored tooling;
  upstream owners maintain those artifacts.
- Runtime health, setup installation and live desktop checks are explicit host
  actions. Never run live setup from a worktree or repoint a host launcher into one.
- Main configuration is linked into the live home, including git/config. A
  comment-only change there still requires the live-integration authorization.
- Preserve pending host work under an open task before removing its source prose.
